arxiv-2008-10116.title: Octonionic Brownian windings
arxiv-2008-10116.creator: Gunhee Cho, Guang Yang
arxiv-2008-10116.description: Abstract . We define and study windings along Brownian paths on octonionic, Euclidean, projective, and hyperbolic spaces which are isometric to 8 8 -dimensional Riemannian model spaces. In particular, the asymptotic laws of these windings are shown to be Gaussian for flat and spherical geometries while the hyperbolic winding exhibits different long-time behavior. 1.

arxiv-2205-15138.description: Abstract . We study satisfiability for HyperLTL with a ∀ ∗ ∃ ∗ \forall^{*}\exists^{*} quantifier prefix, known to be highly undecidable in general. HyperLTL can express system properties that relate multiple traces (so-called hyperproperties ), which are often combined with trace properties that specify functional behavior on single traces.

arxiv-2402-10635.title: ContiFormer: Continuous-Time Transformer for Irregular Time Series Modeling
arxiv-2402-10635.creator: Yuqi Chen, Kan Ren, Yansen Wang, Yuchen Fang, Weiwei Sun, Dongsheng Li
arxiv-2402-10635.description: Abstract Modeling continuous-time dynamics on irregular time series is critical to account for data evolution and correlations that occur continuously. Traditional methods including recurrent neural networks or Transformer models leverage inductive bias via powerful neural architectures to capture complex patterns. However, due to their discrete characteristic, they have limitations in generalizing to continuous-time data paradigms.

arxiv-2503-05048.title: Addressing the Subsumption Thesis: A Formal Bridge between Microeconomics and Active Inference
arxiv-2503-05048.creator: Noé Kuhn
arxiv-2503-05048.description: Abstract As a unified theory of sentient behaviour, active inference is formally intertwined with multiple normative theories of optimal behaviour. Specifically, we address what we call the subsumption thesis: The claim that expected utility from economics, as an account of agency, is subsumed by active inference. To investigate this claim, we present multiple examples that challenge the subsumption thesis.

arxiv-2504-11154.title: SAR-to-RGB Translation with Latent Diffusion for Earth Observation
arxiv-2504-11154.creator: Kaan Aydin, Joëlle Hanna, Damian Borth
arxiv-2504-11154.description: Abstract Earth observation satellites like Sentinel-1 (S1) and Sentinel-2 (S2) provide complementary remote sensing (RS) data, but S2 images are often unavailable due to cloud cover or data gaps. To address this, we propose a diffusion model (DM)-based approach for SAR-to-RGB translation, generating synthetic optical images from SAR inputs.

pmc-11314761.title: Investigation of the Zero-Frequency Component of Nonlinear Lamb Waves in a Symmetrical Undulated Plate
pmc-11314761.creator: Xiaoqiang Sun, Guoshuang Shui, Zesheng Zheng, Haoran Jin, Siyu Liu
pmc-11314761.description: When an ultrasonic pulse propagates in a thin plate, nonlinear Lamb waves with higher harmonics and a zero-frequency component (ZFC) will be generated because of the nonlinearity of materials. The ZFC, also known as the static displacement or static component, has its unique application on the evaluation of early-stage damages in the elastic symmetrical undulated plate.

pmc-11642149.title: Orthopedic Devices for Skeletal Class III Malocclusion Treatment in Growing Patients: A Comparative Effectiveness Systematic Review
pmc-11642149.creator: Angelo Michele Inchingolo, Alessio Danilo Inchingolo, Irma Trilli, Laura Ferrante, Angela Di Noia, Elisabetta de Ruvo, Andrea Palermo, Francesco Inchingolo, Gianna Dipalma, Michele Tepedino, Juan Martin Palomo, Domenico Ciavarella
pmc-11642149.description: Background/Objectives: Skeletal Class III malocclusion (Cl III) presents a significant orthodontic challenge, particularly in growing patients, requiring interceptive treatment to achieve effective functional and aesthetic correction. This review aims to compare various orthopedic devices and therapeutic protocols used in Cl III correction, identifying the most effective options in an interceptive context.

pmc-11674085.title: Food Allergy-Related Bullying in Pediatric Patients: A Systematic Review
pmc-11674085.creator: Rita Nocerino, Caterina Mercuri, Vincenzo Bosco, Greta Aquilone, Assunta Guillari, Silvio Simeone, Teresa Rea
pmc-11674085.description: Background: Food allergy (FA)-related bullying is a significant public health concern affecting pediatric patients. This systematic review investigates the prevalence, characteristics, and psychosocial impact of FA-related bullying, as well as current intervention strategies within educational and healthcare settings. Methods: A systematic literature search was conducted across the PubMed, Web of Science, and CINAHL databases, covering publications up to February 2024.

pmc-13536426.creator: Alqarama Mahardhika Thalib, Khanisyah Erza Gumilar, Bahruddin Thalib, Shang-Ming Wang, Bai-Hung Huang, Jian-Hong Yu, Chung-Ming Liu

pmc-13572840.title: Immigrants’ Gendered Remittance‐Sending Patterns and Purposes: The Role of Marital Status
pmc-13572840.creator: Heather Dicks, Lisa Kaida, Liam Swiss
pmc-13572840.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Research on immigrant remittances and gender is dominated by qualitative studies focusing on specific groups of immigrants; meanwhile, quantitative analysis is scarce due to data limitations. Drawing on the Study on International Money Transfers, a rare survey dataset on remittance behaviours, we compare how immigrant women and men in Canada send money abroad, with a focus on how gender intersects with marital status. We find that married immigrants make some joint decisions regarding remittances.

pmc-13601858.title: A Multicenter Retrospective Comparative Analysis of Therapeutic Outcomes in Multiple Myeloma Patients Receiving Varied Ixazomib Dosage Regimens
pmc-13601858.creator: Liang Zhao, Xiao He, Mingyang Deng, Yun Yuan, Zhiyu Su, Zhongqi Ding, Youping Liao, Chanjuan Shen, Zhongjun Huo, Zimian Luo, Zhiqin Li, Limei Fu, Ping Zhu, Xiangling Feng, Shuping Chen, Yanjuan He, Yan Zhu
pmc-13601858.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMultiple myeloma (MM) is an incurable hematologic malignancy, requiring sustained therapeutic management to mitigate disease recurrence. Ixazomib, a first‐generation oral proteasome inhibitor, has exhibited substantial clinical efficacy and is widely employed in clinical practice. According to prescribing guidelines, ixazomib is typically administered at an initial dose of 4 mg weekly for 3 weeks, with dose reduction to 3 mg weekly in the event of adverse effects.
